root_cause.text: In `drivers/md/dm-mpath.c`’s `parse_path()`, the error path added for a failed `scsi_dh_attached_handler_name()` (-ENOMEM) returned without calling `dm_put_device()` on the already acquired path device, causing a device reference leak in the multipath path-parsing error handling.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the `PTR_ERR(attached_handler_name)` case from `goto bad;` to `goto bad_put_device;`, adds `dm_put_device(ti, p->path.dev);` before freeing the `pgpath`, and the commit message explicitly says the prior fix “didn't clean up the reference to the path device that had just been taken.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix parse_path() error handling to always drop the device reference and report handler-name allocation failures explicitly.
intent_record.what: The error paths in parse_path() were changed so that failures after device acquisition now jump to a new label, bad_put_device, instead of directly to bad. On handler-name allocation failure, ti->error is now set to "error allocating handler name" before branching. A new bad_put_device label was added to call dm_put_device(ti, p->path.dev) and then fall through to the existing bad label, while the previous inline dm_put_device() calls before goto bad were removed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, any failure during handler-name allocation, device handler setup, or path addition now consistently releases the acquired device reference before freeing the pgpath. The change also improves diagnostics for handler-name allocation failures by providing an explicit error message. This prevents device reference leaks on error paths and preserves correct cleanup ordering.
